newsitem.title: USA: Grace to sell polymers business for $147 million.
newsitem.headline: Grace to sell polymers business for $147 million.

text.p: W.R. Grace & Co. said Monday it has agreed to sell its speciality polymers business for $147 million cash to National Starch & Chemical Co.
Grace's speciality polymers business, with manufacturing operations in the United States, Belgium and Japan, had 1996 sales of $73 million.
It makes advanced technology adhesives, coatings, encapsulants and polymer thick films, which are used for circuit and component assembly, and medical and industrial assembly.
The business also produces photopolymers for use in the production of printed circuit boards. It employs about 325 people.

National Starch, based in Bridgewater, N.J., is a worldwide manufacturer of adhesives, resins, speciality chemicals, electronic materials and speciality industrial and food starches. Its annual sales are $2.5 billion.
Grace supplies packaging and speciality chemicals worldwide. Its annual sales are $3.5 billion.
Grace's stock rose 12.5 cents to $56.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
